title: Hello World
statement: Write a program to print Hello, World! on the screen.
outputFormat: Print Hello, World!
hints: Your program needs no input.
Check the exact punctuation and capital letters.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
print("Hello, World!")
```
reference: print("Hello, World!")

title: Add Two Numbers
statement: Given two integers A and B, calculate and print their sum.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers A and B.
outputFormat: Print the sum of A and B.
hints: Read both numbers from one line.
Use split() to separate them.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(a + b)
```
reference:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(a + b)

outputFormat: Print A - B.

A short, direct solution:


title: Even or Odd
statement: Given an integer N, determine whether it is even or odd.
outputFormat: Print Even if N is divisible by 2, otherwise print Odd.
hints: Divide by 2 and look at the remainder.
Zero counts as even.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = int(input())
print("Even" if n % 2 == 0 else "Odd")
```
reference:
n = int(input())
print("Even" if n % 2 == 0 else "Odd")

title: Positive or Negative
statement: Given an integer N, determine whether it is Positive, Negative, or Zero.
outputFormat: Print Positive, Negative, or Zero.
hints: There are three possible answers.
Check for zero separately.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = int(input())
print("Positive" if n > 0 else "Negative" if n < 0 else "Zero")
```
reference:
n = int(input())
print("Positive" if n > 0 else "Negative" if n < 0 else "Zero")

title: Find the Bigger Number
statement: Given two integers A and B, print the greater number. If both are equal, print either number.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers A and B.
outputFormat: Print the greater of the two numbers.
hints: Compare the two numbers.
If they are equal, either one is fine.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(max(a, b))
```
reference:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(max(a, b))

title: Square It!
statement: Given an integer N, calculate and print its square.
outputFormat: Print N multiplied by N.
hints: Multiply the number by itself.
A negative number squared is positive.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = int(input())
print(n * n)
```
reference:
n = int(input())
print(n * n)

title: Count Down
statement: Given a positive integer N, print all integers from N down to 1, separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print numbers from N to 1 in descending order.
hints: Start at N and go down.
Separate the numbers with single spaces.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = int(input())
print(" ".join(str(i) for i in range(n, 0, -1)))
```
reference:
n = int(input())
print(" ".join(str(i) for i in range(n, 0, -1)))

title: Sum from 1 to N
statement: Given a positive integer N, calculate the sum of all integers from 1 to N.
outputFormat: Print the sum from 1 to N.
hints: Add every number from 1 to N.
A loop works; so does the formula N(N+1)/2.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = int(input())
print(n * (n + 1) // 2)
```
reference:
n = int(input())
print(n * (n + 1) // 2)

title: Palindrome Number
statement: A number is called a palindrome if it reads the same forward and backward. Given a positive integer N, determine whether it is a palindrome.
outputFormat: Print Yes if N is a palindrome, otherwise print No.
hints: Compare the number with its reverse.
Print Yes or No exactly.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = input().strip()
print("Yes" if n == n[::-1] else "No")
```
reference:
n = input().strip()
print("Yes" if n == n[::-1] else "No")

title: Multiplication Table
statement: Given an integer N, print its multiplication table from 1 to 10. Print each result on a new line in the format N x i = result.
outputFormat: Print ten lines containing the multiplication table.
hints: Loop i from 1 to 10.
Match the spaces in "N x i = result" exactly.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
n = int(input())
for i in range(1, 11):
    print(f"{n} x {i} = {n * i}")
```

title: Vowel Checker
statement: Given a lowercase English letter, determine whether it is a vowel or consonant. The vowels are a, e, i, o, and u.
outputFormat: Print Vowel or Consonant.
constraints: Input contains exactly one lowercase English letter.
hints: There are exactly five vowels: a, e, i, o, u.
y counts as a consonant here.
editorial:
A short, direct solution:

```
c = input().strip()
print("Vowel" if c in "aeiou" else "Consonant")
```
reference:

print("Vowel" if c in "aeiou" else "Consonant")
